claims.title: Repeated provider delivery can apply a payment mutation twice
claims.content: When the same signed provider event arrives on two workers at nearly the same time, both workers can reach the payment mutation before the existing receipt check completes. A customer-visible payment transition may therefore be applied twice.
claims.summary: Concurrent redelivery can duplicate a payment side effect.

claims.title: A provider event ID may produce side effects once
claims.content: For a Stripe event identifier, at most one worker may execute customer-visible payment mutations. Retries and parallel deliveries must observe the durable claim and return success without repeating the mutation.
claims.summary: Provider event IDs must be idempotent.

claims.title: Claim the event record before payment side effects
claims.content: Insert the provider event ID into PostgreSQL in a transaction before creating or updating payment state. A unique-key conflict means another worker owns or completed the event, so acknowledge the delivery without running the side effect.
claims.summary: Use a durable pre-effect event claim.

claims.title: An in-memory seen-event set might be sufficient
claims.content: The analysis agent assumed one long-running webhook process receives all retries and suggested remembering identifiers in process memory.

claims.title: Receipt insertion already reports ownership
claims.content: The event receipt repository returns acquired=false when its unique insert loses a race, providing the control-flow signal the handler needs without inspecting payment rows.
claims.summary: Receipt insert result identifies the winning worker.

claims.title: Webhook receipts and audit metadata have retention requirements
claims.content: Provider event receipts are operational records, not a transient cache. Keep the event identifier, provider creation timestamp, first-received timestamp, processing outcome, and a non-sensitive failure category for ninety days so support can explain retried deliveries and reconciliation jobs can prove whether an event was claimed. Do not store the complete provider payload in the receipt row because it may contain customer data. Cleanup must run in bounded batches, must never remove records newer than ninety days, and must not race active processing. A cleanup failure must not block webhook handling. This retention rule matters when changing the receipt schema, but the duplicate-processing fix should not add a new cleanup service or broaden payload storage.
claims.summary: Keep minimal receipt audit metadata for 90 days without retaining payloads.

claims.title: Rebuild the catalog search index nightly
claims.content: The catalog index is rebuilt nightly and receives incremental product updates during the day.

claims.title: Receipt email uses approved brand colors
claims.content: Transactional email templates use the approved accessible brand palette.

claims.title: Analytics batches contain 500 events
claims.content: The analytics consumer flushes after 500 product events or thirty seconds.

claims.title: Admin sessions expire after thirty minutes
claims.content: Inactive admin console sessions expire after thirty minutes.

claims.title: Refresh tax rates daily
